audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that Comeuppance is body-blocked. This is the single most important interaction in the matchup and it was absent.
audit.why: Riot's text: Comeuppance "deals damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit." A single minion between Mel and Akshan eats the entire 100-second ultimate. The missing-health scaling also means a healthy Mel takes far less.
audit.corrected: Added to tldr, breakdown.wave, phases[4].why, dosFull[2].d, the Key Ability Interactions row, spikes[2].text and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] read "Reflect Heroic Swing back the moment he commits". Heroic Swing is a grapple and a swing arc, not something that can be sent back.
audit.why: Rebuttal reflects projectiles. Heroic Swing's projectile flag comes from the shots he fires while swinging, not from the movement itself — the engage cannot be reflected.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the terrain requirement, which is the real counterplay.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heroic Swing's two hard conditions are never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: he "fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it" and "gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain." No wall means no engage at all, and a body in his arc ends the swing early.
audit.corrected: Added to winCon, phases[2].why, dosFull[1] and the Key Ability Interactions row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly credits Akshan's shield to his W ("before he has W passive shields") and his camouflage to his passive ("Roam on camouflage passive"). Both are the wrong ability.
audit.why: The shield is Dirty Fighting (P) — every third hit from his attacks and abilities shields him if the target is a champion. The camouflage is the ACTIVE of Going Rogue (W); W's passive is the Scoundrel mark and the ally revive.
audit.corrected: Swapped to the correct abilities in whys[0], whys[4], spikes[0].text and wants.foe[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json (P Dirty Fighting, W Going Rogue)

audit.why: Riot's text: it "deals damage going out and coming back, extending its range each time it hits an enemy." It is a two-pass boomerang that lengthens off every hit, not a single-target poke.
audit.corrected: Named the ability and dropped the single-target claim in whys[0] and spikes[0].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: "your only defensive layer is gone for twenty seconds" understates Rebuttal by roughly half.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 38 seconds at rank 1 in tradeBad, dontsFull[1].d, phases[1].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown section gave no numbers for either of his lane abilities.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 and Avengerang is 9/8/7/6/5. The 18-second swing downtime at rank 1 is the whole step-up window, and it is doubly wide when there is no wall nearby.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2].why and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dirty Fighting's shield cadence is never given, so the text cannot explain why short trades feel bad.
audit.why: Every third hit from his attacks and abilities shields him when the target is a champion, and his attack fires a second reduced-damage shot, so the counter arrives faster than an auto count suggests.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content says Mel pokes "from 950 range" nowhere and repeatedly frames her poke as 550.
audit.why: 550 is her attack range. Radiant Volley casts at 950 and Solar Snare at 1000, both longer than Avengerang's 850 — that gap is the entire reason level 1 is hers.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.early, phases[0].why, dosFull[0].d and tradeGood.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr was the generic "Poke mirror you usually win" line while diff is TRICKY 7/10 and five of seven phases are marked Akshan.
audit.why: The tldr contradicted the file's own difficulty rating and its own level chart.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the Comeuppance body-block, which is the concrete thing that swings the matchup.

edits.after: Comeuppance dies on the first minion in line — keep a body between you.

edits.before: Reflect the poke war in your favour and execute the chip. Keep one eye on Heroic Swing and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Reflect the poke war in your favour and execute the chip. Heroic Swing needs a wall to grapple, so fight in the open lane.

edits.before: Akshan wins by landing Heroic Swing, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Akshan wins by hooking Heroic Swing off a wall, chipping with Avengerang, and owning the spacing war until you starve.

edits.before: Snare through the wave onto his farming spot, fan two full Q volleys while he's locked, and step back with W ready before his answer comes off cooldown.
edits.after: Volley his farming spot from 950 — outside Avengerang's 850 — cast E and W before the auto so all nine projectiles land, then step off his wall.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip damage and then standing in Heroic Swing range — your only defensive layer is gone for twenty seconds.
edits.after: Burning Rebuttal on Avengerang chip and then standing next to a wall — your only defensive layer is 38 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - W Rebuttal is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Akshan Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1 — his engage and his escape, and it needs terrain. Check the walls, not just the timer. - Avengerang is 9s at rank 1. - Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1; chip never gets it.

edits.before: Win the range war from minute one: Q volleys on every last-hit, W held for his one real spell, snare only behind minion cover.
edits.after: Win the range war from minute one: Radiant Volley reaches 950 to Avengerang's 850, W held for his commit, snare only behind minion cover.

edits.before: Best wave: a slow push you tax from max range — he farms inside your snare line and your stacks build toward the execute. Worst wave: frozen near his tower while Heroic Swing is up — you stack nothing and risk everything for each CS. Crash timing: crash on purpose or freeze on purpose; the in-between feeds dives.

Worst wave: no minions between you — Comeuppance stops dead on the first champion, minion or structure it hits, so an empty lane hands him the ultimate back. edits.after: Radiant Volley reaches 950 to Avengerang's 850 — fan it across his last-hit spots and bank Overwhelm early.

edits.after: Rebuttal online, and his kit is nearly all projectiles. But it is 38s at rank 1 — hold it for his commit.

edits.after: Heroic Swing lands at 3: 18s at rank 1, and it must hook terrain. Hold the open lane and he has nothing to grapple.

edits.after: Stack Overwhelm on every step-up, and remember Dirty Fighting shields him on every third hit — burst past it, do not trade into it.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — anyone you've stacked is now walking around with a countdown. Chip, stack, execute.
edits.after: Comeuppance scales on your missing health and dies on the first body it hits. Stay topped up, keep a minion in line.

edits.before: His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Radiant Volley reaches 950 to his 850-range Avengerang — fan it from outside his poke.

edits.after: Level 1 with one ability and a ranged auto you out-poke Avengerang before he has Dirty Fighting shields or Heroic Swing mobility.

edits.after: Roam under Going Rogue's camouflage and snowball side lanes, since he out-ranges your DPS

notes:
Sample size: MC_REAL_GAMES.mel.akshan is 8 games, so the 50% headline is 4 wins in 8 and carries no signal.

The packet defect "never names any of Akshan's abilities" was correct, and while fixing it I found two ability attributions that were simply wrong: the shield belongs to Dirty Fighting (P), not W, and the camouflage belongs to Going Rogue's active, not to his passive. Both are corrected.

Biggest addition: Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure in its path, and its damage scales on the target's missing health. That is in Riot's own text and it was nowhere in either layer. It changes how the lane and the sidelane should be played and it is the reason the tldr was rewritten.

Unfixable under the fixed-length rule: phases[0].side is "Akshan" while content win[0] is "Mel", and the range numbers favour Mel at level 1. A side flip is outside the +/-10% band.

Left alone for lack of a verifiable source: whether Rebuttal's reflect half actually turns Avengerang or Comeuppance around. His kit is projectile-dense so it is very likely, but reflect eligibility is spell-shield class and needsResearch is empty. Every claim I wrote uses only Rebuttal's damage-prevention, which is in Riot's text.
